content: 1. If a vaccine is not administered at the recommended age, it should be given at a subsequent visit. 2. Combination vaccines should be used instead of separate injections when appropriate. 3. Suspected cases of reportable vaccine-preventable diseases must be reported to the state or local health department. 4. For information on precautions and contraindications, refer to the appropriate guidelines or resources. 5. These recommendations must be read in conjunction with the accompanying footnotes. 6. For individuals who are behind schedule or starting late, catch-up vaccination should be provided at the earliest opportunity, as indicated by the relevant guidelines. 7. To determine the minimum intervals between doses, refer to the catch-up schedule. 8. School entry and adolescent vaccine age groups are highlighted in specific sections of the schedule. 9. A vaccine series does not need to be restarted, regardless of the time elapsed between doses. 10. Use the section of the schedule appropriate for the child’s age and always consult the accompanying footnotes. 11. When calculating intervals between doses, 4 weeks is equivalent to 28 days, and intervals longer than 4 months are determined by calendar months. 12. Vaccine doses administered up to 4 days before the minimum age or interval are considered valid. However, doses given 5 or more days earlier than the minimum age or interval are invalid and must be repeated, with the repeat dose spaced according to the recommended minimum interval. 13. Hepatitis B vaccine should be administered within 12 hours of birth, regardless of birth weight. For infants weighing less than 2,000 grams, the vaccine should be given as soon as possible but no later than 7 days of age. 14. The routine Hepatitis B vaccine series consists of 3 doses at 0, 1–2, and 6–18 months. Monovalent Hepatitis B vaccine should be used for doses given before 6 weeks of age. 15. Infants who did not receive a birth dose should begin the series as soon as feasible. 16. Administration of 4 doses is permitted when a combination vaccine containing Hepatitis B is used after the birth dose. 17. The minimum age for the final (3rd or 4th) dose of Hepatitis B vaccine is 24 weeks. 18. Minimum intervals for Hepatitis B vaccine: Dose 1 to Dose 2 is 4 weeks; Dose 2 to Dose 3 is 8 weeks; Dose 1 to Dose 3 is 16 weeks. 19. For catch-up vaccination, unvaccinated individuals should complete a 3-dose series at 0, 1–2, and 6 months. Adolescents aged 11–15 years may use an alternative 2-dose schedule with at least 4 months between doses (adult formulation Recombivax HB only). 20. Rotavirus vaccines have a minimum age of 6 weeks. The Rotarix vaccine is a 2-dose series at 2 and 4 months, while the RotaTeq vaccine is a 3-dose series at 2, 4, and 6 months. If any dose in the series is RotaTeq or unknown, default to a 3-dose series. 21. The rotavirus vaccine series should not be started on or after 15 weeks of age, and the maximum age for the final dose is 8 months. 22. The DTaP vaccine (Diphtheria, Tetanus, and Acellular Pertussis) is a 5-dose series at 2, 4, 6, 15–18 months, and 4–6 years. A 4th dose may be given as early as 12 months if at least 6 months have elapsed since the 3rd dose. 23. For catch-up vaccination, the 5th dose of DTaP is not necessary if the 4th dose was administered at 4 years of age or older. 24. The Hib vaccine (Haemophilus influenzae type b) is administered as a 4-dose series (ActHIB, Hiberix, or Pentacel) at 2, 4, 6, and 12–15 months, or as a 3-dose series (PedvaxHIB) at 2, 4, and 12–15 months. 25. For catch-up vaccination, the schedule varies based on the age at the first dose and the number of doses already received. 26. Special situations for Hib vaccination include chemotherapy, radiation therapy, hematopoietic stem cell transplant, anatomic or functional asplenia, and HIV infection. Specific dosing schedules apply in these cases. 27. The IPV (Inactivated Poliovirus Vaccine) is a 4-dose series at 2, 4, 6–18 months, and 4–6 years. The final dose should be administered on or after the 4th birthday and at least 6 months after the previous dose. 28. For catch-up vaccination, additional doses may be required depending on the age and timing of previous doses. 29. The MMR (Measles, Mumps, and Rubella) vaccine is a 2-dose series at 12–15 months and 4–6 years. The 2nd dose may be given as early as 4 weeks after the 1st dose. 30. For international travel, infants aged 6–11 months should receive 1 dose of MMR before departure, followed by revaccination with 2 doses at 12–15 months and at least 4 weeks later. 31. During a mumps outbreak, individuals at increased risk who have received ≤2 doses of mumps-containing vaccine should receive an additional dose. 32. The Varicella (VAR) vaccine is a 2-dose series at 12–15 months and 4–6 years. The 2nd dose may be given as early as 3 months after the 1st dose. 33. For catch-up vaccination, unvaccinated individuals should receive 2 doses at least 4 weeks apart. 34. The HPV (Human Papillomavirus) vaccine is routinely recommended for adolescents at 11–12 years (can start at age 9) and through age 18 if not previously vaccinated. 35. The number of HPV doses depends on the age at initial vaccination: 2 doses for those aged 9–14 years at 0 and 6–12 months, or 3 doses for those aged 15 years or older at 0, 1–2 months, and 6 months. 36. Special situations for HPV vaccination include starting the series at age 9 for individuals with a history of sexual abuse or assault, and a 3-dose series for immunocompromised individuals aged 9–26 years. 37. The Tdap (Tetanus, Diphtheria, and Acellular Pertussis) vaccine is recommended for adolescents aged 11–12 years, with 1 dose during each pregnancy (preferably at 27–36 weeks gestation). 38. For catch-up vaccination, adolescents aged 13–18 years who have not received Tdap should receive 1 dose, followed by a Td booster every 10 years. 39. Children aged 7–10 years who receive Tdap inadvertently or as part of a catch-up series may still receive the routine Tdap dose at 11–12 years. 40. DTaP given after the 7th birthday may count as part of the catch-up series for children aged 7–10 years or as the adolescent Tdap booster for those aged 11–18 years.
